title: Verifyum Witness Layer checkpoint index version 1
description: One page of published checkpoints, ordered by the period each covers, newest first. Paging uses an exclusive cursor, so a page never repeats a checkpoint already given. It does NOT follow that a walk sees everything: rows are ordered by period, not by publication, and a daily checkpoint is published about twenty-four hours after its period starts, so it appears part-way down the list rather than at the head and a reader who has passed that point will be told `next` is null without having seen it. A reader who needs a complete snapshot compares `total` across the walk and starts again if it moved. Nothing here names a proof; a checkpoint is an aggregate over many.

kind.description: Null when the page mixes both kinds, otherwise the single kind it was filtered to.

limit.description: The page size actually applied, after clamping.

total.description: Every checkpoint matching this filter, counted before the cursor is applied, so it is the same on every page of an unchanged record. If it changes during a walk something was published, possibly below the cursor, and a reader that needs completeness should walk again.

reaches_beginning.description: True when the index can page back to the first checkpoint ever published. False when the listing hit its internal bound, in which case a null `next` means the index has run out rather than the record having ended, and older checkpoints exist that this index cannot reach. Do not read a null `next` as completeness without checking this.

checkpoint_url.description: The checkpoint document itself. Its checkpoint_hash is not the SHA-256 of the bytes served: it is SHA-256 over the UTF-8 prefix verifyum:witness:checkpoint:v1 followed by one newline, then the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the document with the checkpoint_hash member removed. witness-checkpoint-v1 states the rule.

receipts_url.description: What each witness channel attested for this checkpoint.

next.description: The next page, or null when this is the last. The cursor is exclusive, so following it never repeats a checkpoint.
